subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw change unconfigured `memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes` from disabled to a default periodic fallback, or keep periodic sync opt-in and solve watcher resilience through narrower health/recovery behavior?
rationale: The bug is real enough to keep open, but default-on periodic sync changes background filesystem/hash/index/provider work for existing unconfigured users, which repository policy treats as a compatibility-sensitive product decision.

options.title: Approve default fallback after repair
options.body: Repair the open candidate PR so dirty marking is scoped correctly, then accept the default periodic fallback with explicit `0` opt-out and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep interval opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at `0` and instead improve watcher health/error recovery plus docs or doctor guidance for users who want a fallback.

options.title: Require live outage proof first
options.body: Hold the default decision until a live gateway/chokidar outage reproduction shows the fallback is needed beyond the current watcher recovery paths.

recommendation.title: Approve default fallback after repair
recommendation.body: Repair the open candidate PR so dirty marking is scoped correctly, then accept the default periodic fallback with explicit `0` opt-out and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest local history on memory search and the memory-core refactor, making him the best available owner for the memory fallback/default decision.
